terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A parked vehicle prop: an exterior shell with no interior geometry, since a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside and the glazing is authored as a tinted, mostly opaque pane. The wheels are the mechanisms: each is a named pivot on its axle. Nothing else moves and nothing attaches, so there are no sockets. A delivery sidecar: an old green-and-cream underbone with a welded-on cargo box on its left, rusted square tube, planked floor, low rails, four posts carrying a sagging tan canvas canopy, a wire-spoked third wheel outboard of the box.

reasoning: Two machines welded together: an old underbone (cream leg shield and covers, green fenders, nacelle and fork shrouds) on the right and a cargo box on its LEFT -- a rusted tube frame with a planked deck, rails, four posts and a draped canvas canopy, on a third wire-spoked wheel.

Four materials: paint (cream, green and the black saddle as vertex colours), a white vertex-coloured trim (rust tubes, chrome, canvas canopy, engine, lamps), a timber material carrying the plank canvas for the deck, and a rubber material carrying the tread tile for the wheels.
One repetition system: all THREE wheels off one open spoked lathe (tyre ring, rim ring, drum hub, twenty prism spokes), the sidecar wheel as the third instance at 0.923 scale.
Action readiness: three axle pivots, convex collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The sidecar is a CAGE and reads by its gaps: rails on three sides, posts to a canopy, daylight through all of it -- and the wheels are wire wheels that read by the daylight through THEM. It is therefore tubes, a deck and open lathes, and the turntable sees the backdrop through it from every side: the vehicle, not a hole. The bike is the shared underbone template offset to x -0.52.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

The turntable gate's enclosed-background signal fires on the daylight through the cage and the wire wheels from every azimuth: real open air. --allow-holes is set on the _holecc measurement.

preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 1.75 x 1.46 x 1.86 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=4 materials, <=8 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus one named pivot per wheel (3); zero sockets; convex collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

silhouette.description: Bike wheels 0.52 m at z +0.66 and -0.56 on x -0.52 with the fork on an 18 deg rake through the front hub; leg shield 0.31-0.90 m with a flared apron; headlamp nacelle at 0.88 m ahead of the bar clamp, bars at 0.99 m swept 18 cm back; saddle 0.60-0.72 m; rear fender hugging the rear tyre to 0.36 m behind the axle; box deck at 0.34 m from x -0.08 to 0.74 and z 0.38 to -0.67; rails at 0.48 and 0.62 m; posts to 1.28 m; canopy on the top ring with its crown to 1.43 m; sidecar wheel 0.48 m at x 0.80, z -0.34.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -0.875..+0.86 (bike grips to the sidecar wheel face); y 0.00 to 1.455 at the canopy crown; z -0.895..+0.97 rear fender to front tyre, +Z forward. The Meshy proxy normalises to W:H:D = 1.724 : 1.527 : 1.899 = 1 : 0.886 : 1.10, and its side elevation puts the rig at 3.6 wheel diameters long: on a Cub 17-inch wheel (0.52 m) that is 1.87 long, 1.70 wide and 1.50 tall, against the list-time 1.55 x 1.15 x 2.20. A Cub is 1.84 m long; the first build had carried 2.18 m with the rear bodywork 0.70 m behind the rear axle. Rebuilt to the proxy and the declaration corrected to 1.75 x 1.46 x 1.86 (bands.mjs mean |dw| 0.052, |dd| 0.092 of height, from 0.097 / 0.350).
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to W:H:D = 1 : 0.886 : 1.10. Its occupancy map (scratch/sidecar-motorcycle/_ev/occupancy.txt) puts the canopy at z 0.13-0.855 of H over the box posts at columns 37-75 of 80, the bike at columns 5-25, the sidecar wheel outboard at 76-79; the side elevation puts the sidecar hub 0.33 of the box length ahead of its rear. All of that is built; the residual band rows (|dw| <= 0.10, |dd| <= 0.15) are the proxy fusing the bike frame into the box at rail height.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.75: the bike's right side and the box's rear are built to type (exhaust on the right, a canvas valance at the rear).

textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. 3,964/4,000 triangles, 4/4 draw calls, 4/4 materials, 4/8 unique geometries, two canvases at 1.7 MB, factory 82 ms. Turntable: enclosed background is the open cage and the wire wheels, allowed on measurement.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Three components and one repetition system: 4 of 4. The canopy and every fitting ride the trim merge; all three wheels are one InstancedMesh on the rubber material.

materials.note: paint, trim, timber and rubber: 4 of 4.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 3,964 of 4,000: three open wheels at 648 each are half of it; tube runs with buried ends are open-ended to pay for the front end and the canopy sheet.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Thin extrusions for the bike panels and fender arcs, polyline tubes for frame and cage, open ring lathes with prism spokes for the wheels, lathes for the nacelle and pods, a height-grid sheet for the canopy, boxes for deck and fittings.
One InstancedMesh carries all three wheels; the sidecar instance is scaled 0.923.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Every material is declared textureless. One 512 px plank canvas on the timber and one 256 px tyre canvas on the rubber, each as map and bumpMap. 1.7 MB of texture VRAM, factory 82 ms.
